items.quote: I’m not great at delivering ice-breaking activities… or team-building when it involves building a tower from cardboard boxes.
items.statement: I realize I’m not great at delivering ice-breaking activities… or team-building.

items.quote: some of the challenges weren’t just about what I did or didn’t do—they highlighted opportunities to better align training with how things are structured within the companies themselves.
items.statement: Challenges highlighted opportunities to better align training with company structures.

items.quote: If management isn’t in the game, agents slip back into old habits.
items.statement: If management isn’t in the game, agents slip back into old habits.

items.quote: if you’re not using those skills in real client interactions, it’s like learning to swim but never jumping in the pool.
items.statement: Learning new skills without application is ineffective.

items.quote: Sure, you’ve got a CRM, but what about a clear client journey?
items.statement: A CRM alone does not equate to a solid sales strategy.

items.quote: Thinking one week of training will fix everything is like expecting six-pack abs after two trips to the gym.
items.statement: One week of training will not fix everything and requires consistent practice.

items.quote: It’s a whole process—consistent practice, management backing, a clear plan.
items.statement: Effective training requires management backing, a clear plan, and consistency.

overview: A reflective post by a professional discussing personal observations from the past year and insights on effective training methods in sales.
